visual-basic task verified end-to-end with qwen3.8-27b-gsq-rco on gaming-b650 GPU. PASS with 378 prompt tokens including image, 89 completion tokens.

The model achieved a perfect 6/6 pass rate on all tool-use tasks, matching qwen3.8-27b's strong bare result with no failures across the 6 tasks, requiring only a tag-mismatch quirk fix for the host's llama-server.

The `extract-basic` task regressed from a prior 5/6 PASS to a current 4/6 PASS following a mandatory service restart, while `extract-optional` failed on a missing fence around otherwise-correct JSON, a recurring instability seen in a Confirm session on 2026-08-05.
The model achieved 5/6 passes, showing 2 improvements on previously failed tasks while regressing on a new failure, leaving the root cause of the regression uninvestigated.
The model achieved a 6/9 pass rate, improving three previously failed tasks while regressing two others, leaving `reason-trace` and `reason-coverage` unresolved despite the 60% gate being cleared.
The model achieved full success across all six subtasks, with two previously failing cases (tool-none, tool-policy) now resolved by adhering to the exact phrasing requirements of verify.sh.

The model successfully passed all six extract tasks, including previously failing `extract-basic` and `extract-optional`, demonstrating improved stability with 185, 356, 191, 326, 205, and 223 tokens used across the six tasks.
The model improved on two previously failed tasks but regressed on `review-clean`, which now fails despite previously passing.

The model achieved perfect results across all nine document tasks with no failures at n=1, requiring no steering or additional draws.

The model failed three specific reason tasks (reason-config-validity, reason-multihop, reason-tradeoff) while passing six others, yielding a 6/9 pass rate with a single draw. This raw pass/fail count indicates bare performance without idiom classification against task-specific failure idioms.
The model achieved a perfect 6/6 pass rate with no failures at n=1, demonstrating reliable tool-use capabilities across all six tasks.

The model achieved a perfect 6/6 pass rate across all six extract tasks with no failures at n=1, demonstrating consistent performance across basic, optional, multi, classify, ambiguous, and nested scenarios.
The model achieved a perfect 6/6 pass rate across all review tasks, with no failures at n=1.

results.statusLabel: 14/14 PASS, bare, single draw (12 C# + 2 Python tasks), real compile+test via bench.sh
results.finding: The model achieved a perfect 14/14 pass rate across all tasks, marking the first real result for this role on this machine after fixing the dotnet environment, with 13 improvements over the previous report and only one unchanged Python task.
The model achieved a 4/9 pass rate across nine reasoning tasks, with failures in diagnose, trace, consequence, compare, and multihop, while passing config, checklist, tradeoff, and coverage.

The model achieved a perfect 6/6 pass rate across all six tool-use tasks with zero failures at n=1, demonstrating consistent performance across the tool-select, tool-args, tool-multi, tool-none, tool-error, and tool-policy benchmarks.

The model achieved a perfect 6/6 pass rate across all six extract tasks without any failures at n=1, demonstrating consistent performance across basic, optional, multi, classify, ambiguous, and nested scenarios with token counts ranging from 14 to 223 and completion times between 92 and 142.
The model failed on `review-null` and `review-logic` while passing five other tasks, indicating incomplete idiom classification and logic handling.
The model achieved a perfect 14/14 pass rate across all C# and Python tasks, with a total of 208 tokens spent on the first task and 21188 MB of free RAM available before the run.

results.statusLabel: Seven of ten pass with one verifier false negative
results.finding: The model achieved a 7/10 pass rate on the first report, with 3 failures driven by whitespace drift, edit errors, and a verifier mismatch. The doc-audience failure is a false negative where the output correctly stated fact 3 using "can never match" instead of the verifier's expected "cannot match".
The model passes 7 of 10 tasks at low thinking, including 3 that other builds failed. However, low thinking is unsafe without a token cap, as 2 of 10 tasks used more than 15,000 tokens.
